Remark.content: Investigation comprised 5 boreholes (BH-1 through BH-5) and 2 out-of-boundary boreholes (BH-1-OUT, BH-2-OUT), totalling approximately 150 m of drilling. In-situ SPT testing performed throughout. Laboratory testing included Atterberg limits, particle size distribution, CBR, and compaction tests. Foundation system comprises 1,075 controlled modulus columns (CMC/rigid inclusions) across 13 load transfer platform zones.

Site geology comprises surficial aeolian sand overlying medium-dense to dense silty sand and sandy silt, with occasional gravel layers. Groundwater not encountered within the investigated depth. Foundation recommendations based on CMC rigid inclusion system with load transfer platform (LTP) of compacted granular fill.

RIFoundationSystem.gml:description: Rigid Inclusion Foundation System for the Jazera Royal Palace Substation (GBL-GT-24136), Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Comprising controlled modulus columns (CMC) installed through compressible fill and weak near-surface soils, topped by granular load transfer platforms (LTP). System designed to support electrical substation structures and equipment foundations.

Groundwater not encountered during column installation (all boreholes dry to 30 m depth). Construction period: 2024-08-12 to 2024-10-28.

BH-1 Drilling and Completion Record — Jazera

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.
Jazera Royal Palace Development Authority site representative present on site during BH-1 drilling operations. Client approved final borehole termination depth of 30.0 m.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 30.0 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.

Drilling fluid returns observed to be clean and consistent throughout. Cuttings collected at surface at each SPT interval and logged by the attending geotechnical engineer. No refusal encountered above 15.0 m; SPT refusal (N > 50) first recorded at 22.5 m depth.

BoreholeConstructionMethod.holeStability: Stable throughout 30.0 m depth. No caving, no fluid loss, no obstruction. Borehole walls supported by bentonite drilling fluid pressure. Open hole condition maintained without incident from surface to termination depth.

Specification.gml:name: Rotary Wash Drilling — ASTM D5783

Remark.content: Rotary wash method selected as appropriate for anticipated loose to medium dense aeolian sands and silty sand stratigraphy. Water-based drilling fluid with bentonite additive used throughout to maintain borehole stability and return cuttings to surface.

Specification.standardTitle: Standard Guide for Use of Direct Rotary Drilling with Water-Based Drilling Fluid for Geoenvironmental Exploration and the Installation of Subsurface Water-Quality Monitoring Devices

Parameter.parameterValue: potable water with 4–5% bentonite by weight

Specification.gml:name: Standard Penetration Test — ASTM D1586

Remark.content: SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals from 1.5 m to 30.0 m bgl (20 tests total). Automatic trip hammer used. Split-spoon sampler driven in three 150 mm increments; N-value recorded as sum of blows for second and third increments. Samples retained for laboratory index testing.

Specification.standardTitle: Standard Test Method for Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Split-Barrel Sampling of Soils

BH-1 Primary Drill Rig

Remark.content: Rig operated by Global Geosolutions drilling crew under supervision of senior driller. All equipment pre-mobilisation checks completed satisfactorily prior to spud-in.
Beretta T44 crawler-mounted hydraulic rotary rig. Maximum drill depth capability 120 m with NQ rods. Rig performed without mechanical fault throughout BH-1 operations.
Rig mobilised from GGL Riyadh equipment yard on 3 March 2024. Pre-shift daily inspection completed and signed off by senior driller at 06:15 AST on 4 March 2024.

GroutPlant.gml:description: Portable grout plant used for preparation and placement of cement-bentonite grout for borehole backfill completion of BH-1.
GroutPlant.gml:name: GGL Portable Grout Plant No. 2
BH-1 Backfill Grout Plant

Remark.content: Grouting operations commenced at 16:00 AST following completion of final SPT at 30.0 m and withdrawal of drill string. Cement-bentonite grout tremied from base of borehole to surface.
Client representative witnessed grouting operations and confirmed satisfactory completion of borehole backfill prior to demobilisation of rig from BH-1 location.

Portable paddle mixer and diaphragm grout pump used to prepare and place cement-bentonite grout. Grout mix design: OPC 50 kg per 25 litres water with 3% bentonite by dry weight of cement. Specific gravity of grout verified at 1.42 prior to placement.

Grout placed via 25 mm tremie pipe inserted to base of borehole and withdrawn progressively as grout level rose. Total grout volume placed approximately 530 litres. Return of grout observed at surface confirming complete fill of 30.0 m borehole.

GroutMixer.gml:description: Paddle mixer forming part of portable grout plant for cement-bentonite preparation.
GroutMixer.gml:name: GGL Paddle Mixer — BH-1

GroutPump.gml:description: Diaphragm grout pump used to convey cement-bentonite grout from mixer to tremie pipe for borehole backfill placement.
GroutPump.gml:name: GGL Diaphragm Grout Pump — BH-1

GroutPump.gml:description: Secondary diaphragm pump used for positive-pressure tremie grout injection to base of BH-1 during backfill operations.
GroutPump.gml:name: GGL Diaphragm Pump No. 7
BH-1 Tremie Injection Pump

Remark.content: Secondary pump operated by drilling crew to maintain positive pressure during tremie grout injection from borehole base upward.
Pump operated at low flow rate (20–25 l/min) to avoid displacement of settled grout and ensure continuous upward fill without voids.
Equipment inspected and pressure-tested prior to use. No mechanical faults recorded during BH-1 grouting operations.

CoringDevice.gml:description: NQ double-tube wireline core barrel used for selective continuous sampling during BH-1 drilling.
CoringDevice.gml:name: NQ Double-Tube Core Barrel — Unit 07
BH-1 Core Barrel

Remark.content: Core barrel deployed for selective sampling of lithological contacts identified during SPT interval logging. Total core recovery logged and photographed by attending geotechnical engineer.
NQ double-tube wireline core barrel. Plastic liner used to preserve sample integrity. Core runs of 1.5 m conducted at intervals where continuous recovery was specified.
Core barrel inspected prior to use; shoe and inner tube in good condition. No loss of core during retrieval. Core boxes labelled and retained for client archive.

Equipment.gml:description: Automatic trip hammer assembly used for Standard Penetration Testing throughout BH-1 at 1.5 m intervals.
Equipment.gml:name: GGL Automatic SPT Trip Hammer No. 4
BH-1 SPT Hammer

Remark.content: Automatic trip hammer deployed for all 20 SPT tests in BH-1. Hammer energy ratio ER = 72% confirmed by calibration certificate dated January 2024.
GGL automatic trip hammer No. 4. Hammer mass 63.5 kg; drop height 762 mm. Energy ratio ER = 72% per most recent calibration. Split-spoon sampler OD 51 mm, ID 35 mm, compliant with ASTM D1586.
Hammer calibration certificate valid until 31 December 2024. Equipment inspected by engineer prior to first SPT of the day. No malfunctions recorded during BH-1 testing.

GroutInjectionEquipment.gml:description: Tremie pipe grout injection assembly used for placement of cement-bentonite backfill grout from the base of BH-1 upward to surface on completion of drilling operations.
GroutInjectionEquipment.gml:name: GGL 25 mm Tremie Pipe Assembly — Unit 03
BH-1 Tremie Grout Injection Assembly

Remark.content: Tremie pipe inserted to base of borehole at 30.0 m prior to commencing grout injection. Pipe withdrawn progressively as grout level rose. Full grout return confirmed at surface by 17:30 AST.

25 mm nominal bore rigid PVC tremie pipe used for grout injection. Pipe sections coupled with threaded joints and lowered to 30.0 m depth prior to pumping. Grout injected under low positive pressure to avoid hydraulic fracture of borehole walls.

Tremie assembly inspected for blockage prior to use. No blockages or flow interruptions recorded during BH-1 grouting operation. Total elapsed injection time approximately 90 minutes for 530 litre volume.

JetGroutingMonitor.gml:description: Single-fluid jet grouting monitor carried on site during GBL-GT-24136 field operations in connection with RIFS ground improvement works. Not deployed within BH-1 but recorded here as site equipment present during borehole construction.
JetGroutingMonitor.gml:name: GGL Single-Fluid Jet Grouting Monitor — Unit 01
Jazera Site Jet Grouting Monitor — RIFS Works

Remark.content: Jet grouting monitor present on site during borehole drilling operations. Equipment maintained in standby condition for RIFS column installation works commencing following completion of geotechnical investigation phase.
Client acknowledged presence of jet grouting equipment on site. Equipment inventory confirmed by client site representative as part of pre-works mobilisation checklist.

Single-fluid (grout only) jet grouting monitor with single nozzle configuration. Designed for column diameters of 400–600 mm in loose sandy soils consistent with Jazera site stratigraphy. Rotation speed 8–12 rpm; withdrawal rate 50–100 mm/min.
Equipment serviced and pressure-tested prior to mobilisation to Jazera site. Service records held in GGL equipment register GGL-JGM-01-SERVICE-2024.

GroutMixer.gml:description: Standalone high-shear colloidal grout mixer used for preparation of bentonite slurry drilling fluid for BH-1 rotary wash drilling. Separate from the paddle mixer nested within the grout plant used for cement-bentonite backfill.
GroutMixer.gml:name: GGL High-Shear Colloidal Mixer — Unit 02
BH-1 Bentonite Slurry Mixer

Remark.content: Bentonite slurry prepared prior to spud-in at 05:45 AST. Mud weight and Marsh funnel viscosity checked hourly throughout drilling operations and adjusted as required to maintain adequate cuttings return and borehole stability.

High-shear colloidal mixer used to hydrate bentonite powder in potable water. Mix ratio 4–5% bentonite by weight. Slurry hydrated for minimum 30 minutes before use. Marsh funnel viscosity maintained at 35–45 seconds throughout BH-1 drilling.
Mixer inspected and flushed clean prior to mobilisation to site. Motor and impeller in good condition throughout operation. No mechanical faults recorded during BH-1 operations.

CutterSoilMixingTool.gml:description: Cutter soil mixing (CSM) tool present on site in connection with RIFS panel wall construction adjacent to the Jazera Royal Palace Substation footprint. Recorded here as site equipment mobilised concurrently with borehole investigation phase.
CutterSoilMixingTool.gml:name: GGL Bauer CSM Tool — Unit 01
Jazera CSM Panel Wall Tool — RIFS Works

Remark.content: CSM tool mobilised to Jazera site on 4 March 2024 concurrent with geotechnical investigation borehole drilling. Tool held in standby pending completion of investigation phase and RIFS design confirmation.
Jazera Development Authority representative confirmed mobilisation of CSM equipment to site. CSM panel design parameters to be confirmed following receipt of final geotechnical investigation report.

Bauer CSM tool configured for 550 mm wide panel elements. Dual counter-rotating cutting wheels with integrated grout injection ports. Design panel depth 18.0 m for substation perimeter cut-off wall application.
Tool commissioned and pressure-tested on 3 March 2024 prior to mobilisation. Cutting wheel bearings and grout ports inspected and found in serviceable condition.

DeepSoilMixingTool.gml:description: Triple-shaft deep soil mixing (DSM) tool present on the Jazera site for RIFS rigid inclusion column installation. Recorded here as site equipment mobilised during the geotechnical investigation phase.
DeepSoilMixingTool.gml:name: GGL Keller Triple-Shaft DSM Tool — Unit 01
Jazera RIFS Deep Soil Mixing Tool

Remark.content: DSM tool on standby at Jazera site during borehole investigation operations. Tool scheduled for deployment on RIFS column installation commencing following geotechnical investigation sign-off.
Client site representative recorded DSM tool mobilisation as part of site establishment inspection on 4 March 2024.

Triple-shaft DSM tool with 500 mm diameter mixing blades on each shaft at 700 mm centre spacing. Grout injected through hollow shafts via check valves at blade level. Design column diameter 500 mm; design depth 15.0 m into dense silty sand with gravel.
Tool configured for wet method DSM with OPC-based grout at water:cement ratio 0.7 by weight. Target unconfined compressive strength of treated soil-cement columns minimum 1.0 MPa at 28 days.

Sensor.gml:description: Borehole inclinometer probe used to measure deviation of BH-1 from vertical following completion of drilling to 30.0 m depth. Survey confirmed borehole deviation within specified tolerance of 2° from vertical throughout.
Sensor.gml:name: GGL Slope Indicator Inclinometer Probe — Unit 03
BH-1 Post-Drilling Deviation Survey Probe

Remark.content: Borehole deviation survey conducted by GGL geotechnical engineer immediately following completion of final SPT and withdrawal of drill string. Survey readings taken at 1.5 m depth intervals from surface to 30.0 m.
Client representative witnessed borehole deviation survey. Maximum recorded deviation of 1.3° from vertical at 28.5 m confirmed as within the project specification tolerance of 2°.

Slope Indicator digitilt inclinometer probe. Biaxial MEMS accelerometer sensors measuring deviation in two orthogonal planes (A-axis and B-axis). Readings taken at 0.5 m intervals on downhole and uphole passes; results averaged. Maximum deviation 1.3° at 28.5 m depth; all readings within 2° project tolerance.
Probe calibration current to 30 June 2024. Data logger zeroed at surface prior to each survey run. Probe lowered and retrieved on graduated cable; cable depth markings verified against rod tally.

BH-1 CU Triaxial Test Apparatus — GGL Riyadh Laboratory

BoreholeConstructionMethod.gml:description: Full construction method record for BH-1 rotary wash drilling, including all equipment, roles, and procedural remarks for the Jazera Royal Palace Substation geotechnical investigation.
BoreholeConstructionMethod.gml:name: BH-1 Full Construction Method Record
BH-1 Drilling and Completion Record — Jazera

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.
Jazera Royal Palace Development Authority site representative present on site during BH-1 drilling operations. Client approved final borehole termination depth of 30.0 m.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 30.0 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.

Drilling fluid returns observed to be clean and consistent throughout. Cuttings collected at surface at each SPT interval and logged by the attending geotechnical engineer. No refusal encountered above 15.0 m; SPT refusal (N > 50) first recorded at 22.5 m depth.

BoreholeConstructionMethod.holeStability: Stable throughout 30.0 m depth. No caving, no fluid loss, no obstruction. Borehole walls supported by bentonite drilling fluid pressure. Open hole condition maintained without incident from surface to termination depth.

Specification.gml:name: Rotary Wash Drilling — ASTM D5783

Remark.content: Rotary wash method selected as appropriate for anticipated loose to medium dense aeolian sands and silty sand stratigraphy. Water-based drilling fluid with bentonite additive used throughout to maintain borehole stability and return cuttings to surface.

Specification.standardTitle: Standard Guide for Use of Direct Rotary Drilling with Water-Based Drilling Fluid for Geoenvironmental Exploration and the Installation of Subsurface Water-Quality Monitoring Devices

Parameter.parameterValue: potable water with 4–5% bentonite by weight

Specification.gml:name: Standard Penetration Test — ASTM D1586

Remark.content: SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals from 1.5 m to 30.0 m bgl (20 tests total). Automatic trip hammer used. Split-spoon sampler driven in three 150 mm increments; N-value recorded as sum of blows for second and third increments. Samples retained for laboratory index testing.

Specification.standardTitle: Standard Test Method for Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Split-Barrel Sampling of Soils

BH-1 Backfill Grout Plant

Remark.content: Grouting operations commenced at 16:00 AST following completion of final SPT at 30.0 m and withdrawal of drill string. Cement-bentonite grout tremied from base of borehole to surface.
Client representative witnessed grouting operations and confirmed satisfactory completion of borehole backfill prior to demobilisation of rig from BH-1 location.

Portable paddle mixer and diaphragm grout pump used to prepare and place cement-bentonite grout. Grout mix design: OPC 50 kg per 25 litres water with 3% bentonite by dry weight of cement. Specific gravity of grout verified at 1.42 prior to placement.

Grout placed via 25 mm tremie pipe inserted to base of borehole and withdrawn progressively as grout level rose. Total grout volume placed approximately 530 litres. Return of grout observed at surface confirming complete fill of 30.0 m borehole.

Core barrel inspected prior to use; shoe and inner tube in good condition. No loss of core during retrieval. Core boxes labelled and retained for client archive.

Remark.content: Automatic trip hammer deployed for all 20 SPT tests in BH-1. Hammer energy ratio ER = 72% confirmed by calibration certificate dated January 2024.
GGL automatic trip hammer No. 4. Hammer mass 63.5 kg; drop height 762 mm. Energy ratio ER = 72% per most recent calibration. Split-spoon sampler OD 51 mm, ID 35 mm, compliant with ASTM D1586.
Hammer calibration certificate valid until 31 December 2024. Equipment inspected by engineer prior to first SPT of the day. No malfunctions recorded during BH-1 testing.

25 mm nominal bore rigid PVC tremie pipe used for grout injection. Pipe sections coupled with threaded joints and lowered to 30.0 m depth prior to pumping. Grout injected under low positive pressure to avoid hydraulic fracture of borehole walls.

Tremie assembly inspected for blockage prior to use. No blockages or flow interruptions recorded during BH-1 grouting operation. Total elapsed injection time approximately 90 minutes for 530 litre volume.

Client acknowledged presence of jet grouting equipment on site. Equipment inventory confirmed by client site representative as part of pre-works mobilisation checklist.

Equipment serviced and pressure-tested prior to mobilisation to Jazera site. Service records held in GGL equipment register GGL-JGM-01-SERVICE-2024.

BH-1 Bentonite Slurry Mixer

Remark.content: Bentonite slurry prepared prior to spud-in at 05:45 AST. Mud weight and Marsh funnel viscosity checked hourly throughout drilling operations and adjusted as required to maintain adequate cuttings return and borehole stability.

High-shear colloidal mixer used to hydrate bentonite powder in potable water. Mix ratio 4–5% bentonite by weight. Slurry hydrated for minimum 30 minutes before use. Marsh funnel viscosity maintained at 35–45 seconds throughout BH-1 drilling.
Mixer inspected and flushed clean prior to mobilisation to site. Motor and impeller in good condition throughout operation. No mechanical faults recorded during BH-1 operations.

Jazera Development Authority representative confirmed mobilisation of CSM equipment to site. CSM panel design parameters to be confirmed following receipt of final geotechnical investigation report.

Tool commissioned and pressure-tested on 3 March 2024 prior to mobilisation. Cutting wheel bearings and grout ports inspected and found in serviceable condition.

Jazera RIFS Deep Soil Mixing Tool

Client site representative recorded DSM tool mobilisation as part of site establishment inspection on 4 March 2024.

Triple-shaft DSM tool with 500 mm diameter mixing blades on each shaft at 700 mm centre spacing. Grout injected through hollow shafts via check valves at blade level. Design column diameter 500 mm; design depth 15.0 m into dense silty sand with gravel.
Tool configured for wet method DSM with OPC-based grout at water:cement ratio 0.7 by weight. Target unconfined compressive strength of treated soil-cement columns minimum 1.0 MPa at 28 days.

Remark.content: Borehole deviation survey conducted by GGL geotechnical engineer immediately following completion of final SPT and withdrawal of drill string. Survey readings taken at 1.5 m depth intervals from surface to 30.0 m.
Client representative witnessed borehole deviation survey. Maximum recorded deviation of 1.3° from vertical at 28.5 m confirmed as within the project specification tolerance of 2°.

Slope Indicator digitilt inclinometer probe. Biaxial MEMS accelerometer sensors measuring deviation in two orthogonal planes (A-axis and B-axis). Readings taken at 0.5 m intervals on downhole and uphole passes; results averaged. Maximum deviation 1.3° at 28.5 m depth; all readings within 2° project tolerance.
Probe calibration current to 30 June 2024. Data logger zeroed at surface prior to each survey run. Probe lowered and retrieved on graduated cable; cable depth markings verified against rod tally.

Remark.content: Global Geosolutions Ltd mobilised Rig No. 3 to BH-1 location on the morning of 4 March 2024. Drilling commenced at 06:30 AST and was completed by 17:45 AST.
Jazera Royal Palace Development Authority site representative present on site during BH-1 drilling operations. Client approved final borehole termination depth of 30.0 m.

Borehole BH-1 advanced by rotary wash method to 30.0 m bgl. Potable water with 4–5% bentonite used as drilling fluid. SPT conducted at 1.5 m intervals throughout using an automatic trip hammer (ER = 72%). No caving or fluid loss observed. Borehole fully grouted with cement-bentonite on completion.

Drilling fluid returns observed to be clean and consistent throughout. Cuttings collected at surface at each SPT interval and logged by the attending geotechnical engineer. No refusal encountered above 15.0 m; SPT refusal (N > 50) first recorded at 22.5 m depth.

BoreholeConstructionMethod.holeStability: Stable throughout 30.0 m depth. No caving, no fluid loss, no obstruction. Borehole walls supported by bentonite drilling fluid pressure. Open hole condition maintained without incident from surface to termination depth.

Remark.content: CU triaxial tests conducted on three undisturbed specimens from BH-1 between 10 and 18 March 2024 at GGL Riyadh laboratory. Specimens prepared and tested in accordance with ASTM D4767.
Jazera Development Authority notified of laboratory testing programme commencement. Results to be transmitted to client with final geotechnical investigation report.

ELE Tritest 50 load frame with digital control panel. Capacity 50 kN axial load; maximum cell pressure 1700 kPa. Pore water pressure measurement via 1700 kPa capacity pressure transducer. Back pressure saturation applied; B-value ≥ 0.96 confirmed prior to consolidation stage for all three specimens.

Equipment calibration current to 31 December 2024. Load cell, pressure transducers and displacement transducer last calibrated January 2024 by accredited calibration laboratory. Calibration certificates held in GGL laboratory quality management records.
